correctness.rationale: Under the stated nonnegative symmetric kernel, common multiplicative resource-depletion law and nonexplosive process, each original resource component and each corpse deposit has a total consumed-mass budget of at most μ0(R^d) and m respectively. The instantaneous birth intensity paid for by component j is (β/c) times its consumed-mass rate, by Fubini and symmetry of K. A fresh independent unit-intensity Poisson process in each component’s consumed-mass coordinate, stopped before its deterministic budget θ r0 or θ, stochastically dominates all charged births, including ones charged to already-dead resource parents. Assigning potential newborns to these resource parents yields an acyclic independent Poisson(θ) offspring Galton–Watson forest with n0+I roots, I~Pois(θr0), covering the actual individuals injectively. Sampling independent Exp(δ) death lifetimes independently of the potential Poisson offspring gives τ0≤sum_actual lifetimes≤S on every realization, by the occupation integral while a live particle exists. For θ<1, Fθ(z)=z exp(θ(Fθ(z)−1)), z_c=e^{θ−1}/θ, and z_q=δ/(δ−q)<z_c exactly when q<δ(1−θ e^{1−θ}); Markov gives the stated explicit exponential tail and Eτ≤(n0+θr0)/(δ(1−θ)). For θ=1, with z_t=δt/(1+δt), u=1−F1(z_t), the identity −log(1−u)−u=log(1+1/(δt))≥u²/2 implies u≤sqrt(2/(δt)); the Laplace comparison produces the claimed constant sqrt(2)/(1−e^(−1)) t^(−1/2). Independently checked representative PGF domain and q* values for θ=1/4,1/2,3/4. The delicate resource-labelled coupling is the analytic premise; numerical tests do not independently validate the interacting spatial stochastic construction.
